what_it_does: In chip manufacturing, yield refers to the fraction of chips on a wafer that actually work correctly — tiny defects introduced during fabrication can kill a chip. Estimating yield before committing to mass production requires running thousands or millions of simulated variations of the manufacturing process (called Monte Carlo simulation), which is very slow. Existing faster methods (like importance sampling, which concentrates simulation effort on the most failure-prone regions, or machine-learning surrogate models) each have blind spots depending on the circuit design. YieldAgent is a system where several AI language models act as specialists that analyze the circuit's characteristics and past data, then dynamically choose which estimation strategy to apply. It also uses a technique called Retrieval-Augmented Generation — essentially giving the AI access to a searchable knowledge base — so it can draw on relevant engineering know-how, and it uses an automated method to tune the estimation algorithm's settings for each new circuit and manufacturing node.
